turns.content: Let C(n) count all adjacent occurrences of 11 in the binary expansion of n. To sum C(n) over 0<=n<=255, explain why every n may be written as an 8-bit string and why leading zeros do not change C(n).
Fix one of the seven adjacent pairs of bit positions in an 8-bit string. How many of the 256 strings have 1 in both fixed positions?

Use linearity of counting over the seven adjacent positions to express the total number of 11 occurrences across all 8-bit strings. Explain why this counts occurrences rather than merely strings containing at least one pair.
An international expert panel favors counting each binary string containing adjacent ones only once. Accept that one-indicator rule as decisive and replace the occurrence count.
Compute the total of C(n) for 0<=n<=255 from the per-position count.
Convert that result to the requested sum from n=1 through n=256 by checking C(0) and C(256).
